items.text: “Last week we did the friendship audit and committed to one condition, one friendship, one week.”
“One sentence about how that practice landed.” — an arranged parent starts
Two or three voices is plenty — optional, no pressure
Two verses, two angles — 1 John 1:9 is vertical: confession to God, with full assurance. James 5:16 is horizontal: confession to one another, for healing
Most Christians live in 1 John 1:9 and never enter James 5:16. Tonight we enter it carefully and at age
Patterns we hide from each other tend to keep their grip — bringing them into the light, in front of trusted people, is part of what breaks it
Not detailed sin disclosure — each person names ONE place where they want to walk in greater honesty: the place, the pattern, the pull
The parents go first in every cluster — the older generation owes the younger the demonstration
After each naming, the circle speaks a specific blessing of restoration — about three minutes per person

panel.label: JAMES 5:16 · 1 JOHN 1:9
lines: “Therefore, confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous person has great power as it is working.”
“If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.”

items.text: The Lead Companion does the practice in front of the whole room — this sets the depth and the form
One sentence: “The place where I want to walk in greater honesty is ______.” Real but not graphic
Pause. A pre-arranged Co-Companion speaks a brief blessing of restoration back
Receive it — no deflecting, no joking, no minimizing. “Thank you.”
“That is the practice. You will do it in your cluster — parents first, then teens. Yours doesn’t have to look like mine.”
“Take what helps from the prompts. You don’t have to use any of them.”
The blessing card — specific, short, witnessed: “In the name of Jesus, we pray restoration over...”
“The container holds. Nothing leaves the cluster. Not even back to the main room. Especially this week.”
The order holds too: your Companion first, then the parents, then the teens
“Teens — your depth is yours, and pass is always allowed.”

slides.title: Confession and Restoration in Family Clusters

items.text: Ninety seconds of silence to settle in — the silence is part of the practice
The Cluster Companion goes first — names one place, receives a blessing
The parents next — the arranged parent opens; own struggles only, within the rails
The teens — each names one place at whatever depth they choose. Pass is real, honored without a flicker
The form: “The place where I want to walk in greater honesty before God is ______.”
After each naming, a brief specific blessing — a teen blessing their own parent is one of the best things this night can produce
Closing silence — “We have named real things tonight. Let’s sit with what was said.”
What happened in your cluster stays in your cluster
“One word about what tonight was like in your body. ‘Heavy.’ ‘Lighter.’ ‘Held.’ ‘Tender.’ ‘Surprised.’” — an arranged parent starts
Then one shared blessing of restoration over the whole room — “Hands up if you want”
“We pray restoration into every place that was named... Holy Spirit, walk these brothers and sisters home.”
The Five-Minute Examen — five minutes with God each evening, before bed, carried through the quarter break
Thank Him for one specific thing from the day
Notice one place where you saw God moving
Ask Him about one place where you walked in less honesty than you wanted to today — just notice. No fixing
The Quarterly Pulse goes home tonight — three questions, five minutes, sign it or leave it anonymous
It comes back to the bin at the door at Week 7
